newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: YACHTING-STUDIOS LINE UP TO MAKE YACHT RESCUE MOVIE - AGENT.
newsitem.headline: YACHTING-STUDIOS LINE UP TO MAKE YACHT RESCUE MOVIE - AGENT.

text.p: Studios are lining up to make a movie about the against-the-odds survival of two yachtsmen shipwrecked near Antarctica last week, even before the rescue ship docks, an agent working for one of them said on Sunday.

Agent Max Markson said he was negotiating advertising endorsements for British yachtsman Tony Bullimore, who survived four days in an air pocket in his capsized yacht before a frigate arrived on Thursday to find him alive.
"One movie (offer) has come out of Australia but my understanding is that 20th Century Fox are also interested," Markson told Reuters.
A separate production house was interested in making a documentary and an Australian television network had already signed an exclusive deal to cover the reunion of Bullimore and his wife, he said.
The frigate that rescued Bullimore and Frenchman Thierry Dubois is due to dock on Monday.
Markson said he had been acting on instructions from Bullimore's nephew pending the frigate's arrival in Perth.
The yachts of both Dubois and Bullimore capsized in heavy weather.

A Royal Australian Air Force Orion maritime aircraft saved another race competitor, Frenchman Raphael Dinelli, on December 27 when it found him and dropped a life raft a few minutes before his overturned yacht sank.

An Orion found Dubois on Monday on his overturned yacht. As another Orion found Bullimore's boat -- with Bullimore inside, as it turned out -- the Royal Australian Navy dispatched the frigate HMAS Adelaide at best speed to rescue the pair, who were well beyond usual merchant shipping lanes.
Orion aircraft watched over the two boats for three days until the ship picked up Dubois early on Thursday and then steamed on to Bullimore's yacht to discover him alive inside.
